Subject: RE: [EXTERNAL] Fwd: Follow-up: YouTube / NSC Sync on Russia
Yesterday I took a follow-up call from Josh Blumenfeld at YouTube on the question of their policy of
demonetizing Russian accounts and not allowing ads in Russia.
Josh relayed that for some time Google/YouTube has funded Ukrainian media outlets through the European
Journalism Center. EJC in turn provides grants to media outlets to supplement their income. He indicated
that funding provides financial support to roughly 40-50 Ukrainian outlets.
Josh indicated that under a newly signed agreement with EJC, Google funding will soon begin to enable
grants to Russian independent outlets. Beyond Dohdz he didn't specify to whom the funds would flow, and
ultimately grant-making decisions rest with EJC, but he indicated that funds would cover all the outlets that
we've raised previously and that he would come back to us with a list of covered outlets once grants are
I also raised the message I heard from Volkov in Vilnius that lack of ability to advertise in Russia is hurting
Team Navalny's ability to attract new Russian viewers. Josh indicated that he'd revert if they could do
anything on this score, notwithstanding general policy that ads can't run in Russia. I relayed Volkov's view
that YouTube is too big to fail in Russia not for its propaganda value, but because of its

mollifying/entertainment value with the Russian population. Josh indicated that that's essential YouTube's
view as well.
. Forwarded message -

Date: Tue, Oct 4, 2022 at 12:22 PM
Subject: RE: Follow-up: YouTube / NSC Sync on Russia

Reynolds, Nate L. EOPINSC < [opaque block] [contact omitted]>, Bradbury, Katherine E. EOP/NSO
[opaque block] [contact omitted]>, Deming, Sasha S. EOP/NSC < [opaque block] [contact omitted]>,
Hateez, Sahar J. EOPINSC < [opaque block] [contact omitted]>
Leslie and team,
To add to Tim's note, we recognize that the list below includes both media enterprises (e.g., Meduza, Rain)
and NGOs (e.g., FRF, Golos). As we discussed during our meeting, to generalize, there are differences in
these two groups funding models, with the former more reliant on advertising revenue and the latter less so.
So while we're consistently hearing from all involved that demonetization has had an inadvertent yet
negative impact, we're particularly interested in what light your data might be able to shed on revenue loss
concerning the former group.
Thanks again, and looking forward to discussing further with you.
Best,
Rob
Rob Berschinski
Special Assistant to the President
and Senior Director for Democracy and Human Rights
National Security Council

Subject: Follow-up: YouTube7 NSC Sync on Russia
Dear Leslie, Ilya, Josh, Clem, and Cris,
Many thanks for connecting with us ten days ago. We greatly appreciated the opportunity to discuss the
series of issues that have been top of mind for us.
Following your suggestion, please find below a preliminary list of organizations affected by the
demonetization in Russia:
• The Insider
• Proyekt/Agenstvo
• iStories
• 7x7
• Meduza
• TV Rain
• Team Navalny
• Free Russia Foundation
• Golos
Please let us know ifyou have any questions and we look forward to hearing from you.
Best,
Tim
Dr. Tim Maurer
Director for Technology and Democracy
Democracy and Human Rights Directorate
National Security Council, The White House
